| `eval/` | Recall on injected synthetic campaigns, false-positive rate on organic bursts, on held-out hours → `eval_runs`. In review (PRs #9, #10). |
| `api/` | FastAPI: clusters, cluster detail, metrics, health, ad-hoc `POST /api/analyze`. |
| `web/` | Dashboard served by Caddy (`web/public/index.html` is a placeholder until the dashboard lands). |
| `common/` | Shared settings (`common.config`) and DB connections (`common.db`), migrations runner. |
| `db/` | `schema.sql` plus `migrations/`. |
| `deploy/` | Docker Compose, Caddy, deploy and outside-check scripts for the Hostinger VPS. |

cat >> lookup/README.md <<'EOF'

## Rules that keep it honest (and why)

- **Times.** X post times come from the post id (snowflake), so every X post found, even one
  only seen in a search result, has its exact creation time. Bluesky times are the record's
  `createdAt`. Web pages get the publisher's date when the scrape extracts one, otherwise the
  search engine's hint ("3 hours ago" relative to the search) marked `search_hint`.
- **Counts.** X hides zero counts on the logged-out page, so a missing number is `null`, never
  0. Counts are what the page showed at `metrics_as_of`.
- **Copies are verified.** A search hit only says the text appears there. Up to
  `LOOKUP_VERIFY_MAX` candidate X posts are read on their own page: a quote of the post, a
  reply to it, or a copy of its words (similarity = share of the post's words the copy
  carries). On 13 Nov 2026 the top "copy" hit for a viral joke was in fact a quote post.
  X hits sharing under 35% of the words are dropped (search engines match loose keywords).
- **Images.** Nemotron reads the post's own images; their text (8+ words) is searched like the
  post text. Link-card thumbnails are described but not searched (their text is a photo label).
  A post that is only an image is searched by the text inside it.
- **Short links** (t.co etc.) are resolved before the page is scraped.
- **No verdict from a footprint.** `status` is `matched` only when the monitor's database has a
  cluster with the link, text or Bluesky accounts. Gemini's `llm_reading` is shown as its
  reading, never as the status, and keeps only citations of receipts that exist.

## Try it

```bash
uv run uvicorn api.main:app --port 8005          # needs OXYLABS_WEB_API_KEY; GEMINI/VERDA optional
curl -s -XPOST localhost:8005/api/lookup -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"url":"https://x.com/StephenKing/status/2121360054330986967"}' | jq .id
curl -s localhost:8005/api/lookup/<id> | jq '.state, .steps[] | {id, state, detail}'
```

A typical X post lookup makes 8-20 Oxylabs calls (1 post page, 1-5 profiles, 4 searches, up
to 8 copy pages, 1 linked page), 0-2 Nemotron calls and 1 Gemini call, in 20-40 s.
EOF

input.title: Sol review r1: dev/lookup link lookup
input.task:
Code review, READ-ONLY: don't edit, commit, push or deploy. Never print secrets (`.env` in the worktree is a symlink to team keys; don't read it).

Repo: gemini-4-braincells ("Shill or Chill", Junction 2026, Hostinger "Decode the Noise": detect coordinated amplification, explain with evidence, honest error rates; judged mostly on honesty of detection logic and false-positive handling). Worktree: `/srv/junction-espoo/gemini-4-braincells.worktrees/dev-lookup`, branch `dev/lookup`. Review the diff `git -C <worktree> diff origin/main...HEAD` (ignore the generated build output under `web/public/trackdown/assets/`).

What the branch adds: a link lookup. `POST /api/lookup` starts a background job (in-process, `lookup/jobs.py`) that traces a link with live data: Oxylabs Web API `/scrape` (markdown) of X post pages and profiles, parsed in `lookup/xpage.py`; `/search` for the exact text on the web / `site:x.com` and for coverage; verification of candidate X copies by reading their own pages; Bluesky public AppView (`lookup/bsky.py`); Nemotron VL on post images (`media/nemotron.py` client, reused); DB check against monitored clusters (`api/store.py`); Gemini reading with a citation guard (`lookup/assess.py`). Orchestration: `lookup/service.py`. Contract: `lookup/README.md`. Route: `api/routes/lookup.py`. Frontend: `web/trackdown/src/data/lookup.ts` + changes in `web/trackdown/src/{main.ts,ui/*,types.ts,data/api.ts}`, Caddy route in `deploy/Caddyfile`, landing page `web/public/index.html`. Tests: `tests/test_lookup.py` (`cd <worktree> && .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/test_lookup.py`; the full suite `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q` should pass too). Trackdown builds with `cd web/trackdown && npm run build`.

Focus, in priority order:
1. Correctness bugs: thread-safety of the shared `LookupResult` (steps run in a ThreadPoolExecutor and the API snapshots mid-run), races between steps (post vs author vs copies order), merge logic in `add_post`, origin/spread computation in `_finish_graph`, X markdown parsing edge cases (zero counts hidden, quotes, replies, truncated text, escaped underscores in handles), snowflake time, job store expiry/caching/rate limits, error paths (Oxylabs failures, DB down, deleted posts).
2. Honesty: anything shown as a fact that isn't one (guessed counts or times, a copy that is really a quote, a verdict implied from one link's footprint, Gemini text presented as a verdict, wording that calls an account a shill/bot). Status must be `matched` only via monitored clusters.
3. Security/cost abuse on a PUBLIC endpoint: SSRF (Oxylabs fetches the URL, but the server itself downloads media images and resolves short links with httpx: check what URLs reach httpx), unbounded memory, rate-limit bypass (X-Forwarded-For trust: the app sits behind Traefik and Caddy on the VPS), XSS in the frontend rendering of scraped text/URLs (check every place scraped strings or URLs go into innerHTML / href; `javascript:` URLs), job id guessing.
4. Frontend/backend contract mismatches.

Report: a ranked list of findings, each with file:line, a concrete failure scenario, and a suggested fix. Mark each as must-fix (bug/security/honesty) or nice-to-have. Say explicitly if you find nothing serious. Keep it concise.

input.title: Astra: Nemotron evidence into Gemini + logging + checks
input.task:
You work on "Shill or Chill" (repo gemini-4-braincells; Junction 2026, Hostinger "Decode the Noise": detect coordinated amplification on Bluesky, explain it with evidence, honest error rates). It is entered in NVIDIA's "Best Use of Nemotron" challenge: Nemotron 3.5 **Super VL** must be in core functionality, visible in the demo, every model call logged (model id, latency, tokens). You are in your own git worktree (a new checkout from the parent commit). First run `git fetch origin main && git checkout -b dev/nemotron-core origin/main` (if the fetch fails on unreadable objects in the shared store, use `git checkout -b dev/nemotron-core origin/main` with the existing ref). Commit your work on that branch with clear messages (end each with a line `Co-Authored-By: Codex (gpt-6-astra) <noreply@openai.com>`); do NOT push, open PRs, merge or deploy: the parent does that. Never print secrets; `.env` files hold team keys (to run the app use `ln -s /srv/junction-espoo/secrets/team.env .env` in your worktree; never cat it). Python env: `uv sync` then `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q`.

Read first: `media/README.md`, `media/nemotron.py`, `media/worker.py`, `analyst/prompt.py`, `analyst/context.py`, `analyst/guard.py`, `analyst/README.md`, `deploy/check.sh`, `tests/test_media*.py`, `tests/test_analyst*.py`.

An audit found these gaps; fix them, smallest complete change each, with tests:

1. **Gemini sees too little of Nemotron's output.** The analyst prompt gets media evidence only as its 200-char summary + URL (`media/worker.py` Finding.summary ~line 74, `analyst/prompt.py` ~line 43). Add a media-specific formatter in the analyst prompt/context so each `evidence(kind='media')` row is shown to Gemini with: model id, a compact description, the relevant OCR lines (bounded, e.g. up to ~600 chars), reuse cues, manipulation cues, n_accounts / n_posts, and for `detail.type=='ocr_template'` rows the shared tokens, the varying tokens and n_images/n_accounts. Keep the evidence id so Gemini can cite it, and keep total prompt size bounded. Mention in the system/user prompt that media evidence comes from Nemotron 3.5 Super VL reading the images and may be cited like other evidence (but OCR text is not proof of who made it). The guard must still accept citations of media evidence ids. Add a test that a media row's OCR and template tokens reach the prompt and that a verdict citing a media evidence id passes the guard.
2. **Every Nemotron call logged, including failures.** In `media/nemotron.py` `_complete` (~line 300-360), log one consistent record per attempt: requested model, returned model (or None), latency_ms (also on failure), prompt/completion tokens when present (None otherwise), finish_reason, attempt number, outcome (ok / retry / error type). In `media/compare.py` make its calls go through the same logging (or log the same fields) and keep prompt-token counts. Test with a fake OpenAI client that a failed attempt logs latency and outcome.
3. **Strict model guard.** `is_vl_model` accepts any id with a `vl` token. Add `is_super_vl_model(model_id)` that requires Nemotron + Super + VL (e.g. `nemotron-3.5-super-vl`, `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-NVFP4`, `nvidia/nemotron-3.5-super-vl-120b-a12b`), and use it where the worker refuses non-VL responses (keep `is_vl_model` for compatibility). Tests for accepted/rejected ids.
4. **Deploy check covers media.** `deploy/check.sh` accepts a site with no media work. Add a soft check (warning line, not a failure, because quiet hours can have no candidate media) that prints the count of clusters with media evidence among the latest ~50 clusters via the public API (`/api/clusters?limit=50` then a few `/api/clusters/{id}` details, `jq` if available else python3), and a hard check that `/trackdown/` returns HTML (status 200 and contains `<div` or `<script`). Keep the script POSIX/bash, no secrets.
5. Update `media/README.md` (a short "Where Nemotron is used" section: candidate-cluster worker → evidence rows → dashboard + Gemini prompt; and the link lookup (`lookup/` on branch dev/lookup, being merged: it sends the images of any submitted X/Bluesky post to Nemotron and searches the OCR text to find where a screenshot circulates). Also fix the README's sample-breakdown arithmetic if it doesn't add up (an audit noted 13 images + 13 videos + 2 quote-media = 28, not 30; check `media/compare.py` / the README to state the true breakdown, don't invent numbers).

Do not touch `signals/`, `ingest/`, `db/`, `eval/`, `web/`, `lookup/`. Run `.venv/bin/ruff check` and `.venv/bin/ruff format` on files you change, and the full test suite. Report: commits (sha + subject), what changed, test results, and anything you could not do.

I'm doing a quick security check on SSRF while I wait: media URLs come from X page parsing, restricted to pbs.twimg.com, and from Bluesky's CDN response, which I'm treating as fairly trusted. For the resolver, I'm only issuing HEAD requests on shortener domains with redirects followed, so I'm checking whether a final redirect could land on an internal IP.

I'm going through redirect handling now: if a shortener's final hop lands on an internal address, the HEAD request would reach it from our server. The fix is to stop following redirects past the first hop, read the Location header instead, and add an allowlist for media hosts (pbs.twimg.com, cdn.bsky.app, video.bsky.app).

While both run, I'm closing an SSRF gap: short-link resolution followed redirects from our server, so a bit.ly link to an internal address could make the VPS request it. I'm switching to reading only the first Location header and allowlisting the media download hosts.

**Found must-fix correctness and honesty issues** at `10e257e`, ranked below.

1. **Must-fix — fabricated engagement counts.** [`lookup/xpage.py:189`](/srv/junction-espoo/gemini-4-braincells.worktrees/dev-lookup/lookup/xpage.py:189): positional assignment cannot identify which zero-count slots disappeared. Reproduction: a likes-only `35K` tail becomes **35,000 reposts**, likes unknown. Preserve ambiguous counts as unknown, or extract labeled metrics rather than guessing their positions.

2. **Must-fix — unverified search hits become copies and origins.** [`lookup/service.py:789`](/srv/junction-espoo/gemini-4-braincells.worktrees/dev-lookup/lookup/service.py:789): web-only hits, candidates beyond `verify_max`, and failed verification retain `role="copy"`. `_finish_graph` includes them in spread and origin selection. Reproduced an unverified hit becoming the origin. Keep these as candidates; exclude them from confirmed copy statistics until verified.

3. **Must-fix — unrelated account membership supplies the link’s verdict.** [`lookup/service.py:1144`](/srv/junction-espoo/gemini-4-braincells.worktrees/dev-lookup/lookup/service.py:1144), [`data/lookup.ts:232`](/srv/junction-espoo/gemini-4-braincells.worktrees/dev-lookup/web/trackdown/src/data/lookup.ts:232): a discovered copier’s membership in an unrelated coordinated cluster produces `matched`, then the frontend inherits that cluster’s verdict. Return match provenance; handle-only matches should be contextual evidence, not a verdict on this link.

4. **Must-fix — late snippets overwrite verified evidence.** [`lookup/service.py:215`](/srv/junction-espoo/gemini-4-braincells.worktrees/dev-lookup/lookup/service.py:215): `old.role == "mention"` permits replacement regardless of verification quality. Reproduced a verified mention becoming an unverified copy after a later search hit. Make verified evidence dominate snippets independently of role.

5. **Must-fix — monitor checks race their inputs.** [`lookup/service.py:351`](/srv/junction-espoo/gemini-4-braincells.worktrees/dev-lookup/lookup/service.py:351): `_monitor` runs alongside Bluesky discovery and linked-page resolution. Reproduced a completed lookup with a matching handle discovered afterward but never checked. Run monitoring after those producers finish, or reconcile newly discovered keys before finalization.

6. **Must-fix — quote edges name the wrong source.** [`lookup/service.py:921`](/srv/junction-espoo/gemini-4-braincells.worktrees/dev-lookup/lookup/service.py:921): matching quoted text is enough to draw a quote edge from the submitted post, even when `quoted_id` identifies another post. Reproduced this misattribution. Connect to the actual quoted ID; text similarity alone establishes no quote relationship to the submission.

7. **Must-fix — date-only hints establish false chronology.** [`lookup/service.py:1180`](/srv/junction-espoo/gemini-4-braincells.worktrees/dev-lookup/lookup/service.py:1180): a search date becomes midnight and can outrank a same-day X post as “origin.” Reproduced this with `Nov 13, 2026` versus a 21:50 post; the page could actually be later. Represent date precision and require non-overlapping time ranges before asserting precedence.

8. **Must-fix — the time budget does not stop work or spending.** [`lookup/service.py:333`](/srv/junction-espoo/gemini-4-braincells.worktrees/dev-lookup/lookup/service.py:333): timed `wait` calls do not terminate workers; executor exit waits for them, downstream work still starts, and assessment has no deadline gate. Reproduced downstream calls starting after expiry. Check deadlines before scheduling/calling providers, bound request timeouts, and cancel queued work.

9. **Must-fix — deployed per-client limiting collapses visitors together.** [`api/routes/lookup.py:84`](/srv/junction-espoo/gemini-4-braincells.worktrees/dev-lookup/api/routes/lookup.py:84), [`deploy/Caddyfile:5`](/srv/junction-espoo/gemini-4-braincells.worktrees/dev-lookup/deploy/Caddyfile:5): Caddy has no trusted-proxy configuration. Its default ignores incoming forwarded headers, so behind Traefik the limiter sees the proxy IP: ten distinct lookups can block everyone. Configure a narrowly trusted, sanitized proxy chain and derive client identity from it. citeturn878393view1

10. **Must-fix — escaped avatar handles look like missing posts.** [`lookup/xpage.py:20`](/srv/junction-espoo/gemini-4-braincells.worktrees/dev-lookup/lookup/xpage.py:20): changing the fixture’s avatar label to `@ada\_example` makes `page.main` disappear. Normalize Markdown escapes in handle labels before matching; add escaped-label fixtures.

**Validation:** lookup tests **11 passed**; full suite **267 passed, 8 skipped**; TypeScript `--noEmit` passed. `.env` loading was disabled. No edits, build output, paid calls, or deployments. No confirmed SSRF or XSS found in the inspected paths.

I'm going through the ten review fixes one at a time, starting with the counts. (the one with a full date link, "[9:50 PM · Nov 13, 2026](/handle/status/ID)"), then replies.
A profile page has the profile header, then the account's recent posts as the same items.

Counts: X hides zero counts, so a missing number is shown by the page as nothing at all. The
post itself shows replies (link), reposts, likes, bookmarks, with views next to the date; other
items show replies (link), reposts, likes, views. When fewer numbers are shown we fill them in
that order and leave the rest None (a hidden count is most often 0, but we don't claim it).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

def _linked(self, url: str, is_input: bool) -> None:
        with self.step("linked") as st:
            short = url
            url = self._resolve(url)
            facts = self.deps.oxylabs.scrape_facts(url)
            call = dict(self.deps.oxylabs.last_call)
            pub = facts.published_at
            ptime = None
            if pub:
                try:
                    ptime = datetime.fromisoformat(pub.replace("Z", "+00:00"))
                    ptime = ptime if ptime.tzinfo else ptime.replace(tzinfo=UTC)
                except ValueError:
                    ptime = None
            rid = self.receipt(
                "oxylabs",
                "/scrape",
                f"Linked page read: {facts.publisher or domain(facts.final_url)}"
                f" — {facts.headline or 'no headline'}" + (f" (published {pub})" if pub else ""),
                source_url=facts.final_url or url,
                call=call,
            )
            pg = self.add_page(
                Page(
                    id="",
                    url=short if short != url else url,
                    final_url=facts.final_url or url,
                    role="linked",
                    publisher=facts.publisher,
                    author=facts.author,
                    published_at=pub,
                    headline=facts.headline,
                    claims=facts.claims,
                    time=ptime,
                    time_source="page" if ptime else None,
                    receipt_id=rid,
                )
            )
            if is_input:
                self._subject_text = self._subject_text or facts.headline
                self._card_title = facts.headline
                self._subject_time = ptime
                with self.lock:
                    self.result.subject_id = pg.id
            elif self.result.subject_id:
                self.add_edge(pg.id, self.result.subject_id, "link", note="the post links it")
            st.found = [pg.id]
            st.detail = f"{facts.publisher or domain(facts.final_url)}: {facts.headline or '-'}"

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- searches
    def _search(self, query: str, n: int = 10):
        hits = self.deps.oxylabs.search(query, max_results=n)
        return hits, dict(self.deps.oxylabs.last_call)

    def _phrase(self) -> str | None:
        return textsim.phrase(self._subject_text) or textsim.phrase(self._card_title)

    def _classify_hit(
        self, hit, rid: int, at: datetime, *, reference: str, min_sim: float = 0.0
    ) -> str | None:
        """Turn one search hit into a post or page; returns the new node id.

        X hits that share few words with the reference are dropped (search engines match loose
        keywords); pages below `min_sim` too."""
        snippet = textsim.strip_snippet(hit.snippets[0]) if hit.snippets else ""
        if m := X_STATUS_RE.match(hit.url):
            handle, sid = m.group(1), m.group(2)
            pid = f"x:{sid}"
            if pid == self.result.subject_id:
                return None
            name, own = _x_title(hit.title)
            sim_own = textsim.similarity(own, reference, truncated=True) if own else None
            sim_snip = textsim.similarity(snippet, reference, truncated=True) if snippet else 0.0
            sim = sim_own if sim_own is not None else sim_snip
            if max(sim, sim_snip) < max(min_sim, X_MIN_SIM):
                return None
            role = "copy" if sim >= COPY_MIN and sim_own is not None else "mention"
            post = self.add_post(
                Post(
                    id=pid,
                    platform="x",
                    url=x_post_url(handle, sid),
                    author_handle=handle,
                    author_name=name,
                    text=own or snippet,
                    created_at=snowflake_time(sid),
                    time_source="snowflake",
                    role=role,
                    similarity=round(sim, 2),
                    receipt_id=rid,
                )
            )
            return post.id
        if _BSKY_POST.match(hit.url):
            return None  # Bluesky copies come from its own search (exact times, API data)
        if re.match(r"https?://(?:www\.)?(?:x|twitter)\.com/", hit.url):
            return None  # profile or search pages, not posts
        sim = textsim.similarity(snippet, reference, truncated=True) if snippet else 0.0
        if sim < min_sim:
            return None
        t = snippet_time(hit.snippets[0] if hit.snippets else "", at)
        pg = self.add_page(
            Page(
                id="",
                url=hit.url,
                role="reference" if sim >= COPY_MIN else "coverage",
                headline=hit.title or None,
                snippet=snippet[:300] or None,
                published_hint=hit.published_hint.isoformat() if hit.published_hint else None,
                time=t,
                time_source="search_hint" if t else None,
                receipt_id=rid,
            )
        )
        return pg.id

    def _copies_web(self) -> None:
        phrase = self._phrase()
        if not phrase:
            self.skip("copies_web", "text too short for an exact-phrase search")
            return
        with self.step("copies_web") as st:
            q = f'"{phrase}"'
            hits, call = self._search(q)
            at = _now()
            rid = self.receipt(
                "oxylabs",
                "/search",
                f"Web search for the exact text: {len(hits)} results",
                query=q,
                call=call,
            )
            ref = self._subject_text or phrase
            st.found = [i for h in hits if (i := self._classify_hit(h, rid, at, reference=ref))]

def _monitor(self) -> None:
        if not self.deps.store:
            self.skip("monitor", "database not configured")
            return
        with self.step("monitor") as st:
            from signals.textnorm import normalize_url

            urls = {u for u in (self.result.input.url, self._card_url) if u}
            with self.lock:
                urls |= {
                    pg.final_url for pg in self.result.pages if pg.role == "linked" and pg.final_url
                }
            variants = sorted({v for u in urls for v in (u, normalize_url(u)) if v})
            phrase = textsim.phrase(self._subject_text)
            found: dict[int, Any] = {}
            try:
                store_cm = self.deps.store()
                store = store_cm.__enter__()
            except Exception as exc:  # DB down: say so, don't fail the lookup
                log.warning("lookup monitor: database unreachable: %s", type(exc).__name__)
                with self.lock:
                    st.state, st.detail = "skipped", "monitor database unreachable right now"
                return
            try:
                if variants:
                    found.update((c.id, c) for c in store.clusters_for_url(variants))
                if phrase:
                    found.update((c.id, c) for c in store.clusters_for_text(phrase))
                for h in list(self._bsky_handles)[:10]:
                    found.update((c.id, c) for c in store.clusters_for_handle(h))
            finally:
                store_cm.__exit__(None, None, None)
            self.receipt(
                "detector", "db", f"Monitored clusters checked: {len(found)} match", query=phrase
            )
            with self.lock:
                self.result.clusters = [c.model_dump(mode="json") for c in found.values()]
                if found:
                    self.result.status = "matched"
            st.detail = (
                f"in {len(found)} monitored cluster(s)"
                if found
                else "not in the Bluesky clusters we monitor"
            )

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- graph + assess
    def _finish_graph(self) -> None:
        with self.lock:
            posts = self.result.posts
            subj = next((p for p in posts if p.id == self.result.subject_id), None)
            # posts that carry the submitted text, oldest first
            carriers = sorted(
                (
                    p
                    for p in posts
                    if p.created_at
                    and p.role in ("submitted", "copy", "bluesky")
                    and (p.similarity or 0) >= COPY_MIN
                ),
                key=lambda p: p.created_at,
            )
            origin_id = carriers[0].id if carriers else self.result.subject_id
            origin_t = carriers[0].created_at if carriers else self._subject_time
            # a page that carries the text and is clearly older than every post is the origin
            older = sorted(
                (
                    pg
                    for pg in self.result.pages
                    if pg.role == "reference"
                    and pg.time
                    and origin_t
                    and pg.time < origin_t - timedelta(hours=1)
                ),
                key=lambda pg: pg.time,
            )
            if older:
                origin_id = older[0].id
                if carriers:
                    self.add_edge(
                        origin_id, carriers[0].id, "cites", note="older page with the same text"
                    )
            self.result.origin_id = origin_id
            if carriers and carriers[0].role == "copy" and carriers[0].id == origin_id:
                carriers[0].role = "origin"
            for p in carriers[1:]:
                self.add_edge(
                    carriers[0].id,
                    p.id,
                    "copy",
                    sim=p.similarity,
                    tool="bluesky" if p.platform == "bluesky" else "oxylabs",
                    note="same text, later",
                )
            if subj:
                for pg in self.result.pages:
                    if pg.role in ("coverage", "reference") and pg.id != origin_id:
                        self.add_edge(subj.id, pg.id, "cites", note="same story")
            self.result.spread = _spread(carriers)
            if any(p.platform == "x" for p in posts):

I'm checking provenance in the finish_graph step: carriers need to be verified, with Bluesky posts counting as verified, the subject verified, and copies from verify verified. I'm adding a `p.verified` requirement, and image-only Bluesky posts are fine. Then I'm moving on to the DB query timeouts, where the connect timeout is 3 seconds and that looks okay.

I'm working out the time budget for the assess step: if the search phases run long, skipping assess would be a loss, so I'm giving it a reserve of its own. The plan is to have the provider calls stop by 125 seconds out of 150, and to check the remaining time against both the call's own need and that reserve.

On the VPS, Traefik (host network, default forwardedHeaders, i.e. untrusted client headers are not passed on) proxies to Caddy on the Docker bridge; Caddy has no host ports there. **Found two must-fix evidence-integrity issues.** Reviewed `origin/main...HEAD` at `b83b55f`. Tests: **299 passed, 8 skipped**; `bash -n deploy/check.sh` passed. Worktree remains clean.

### Ranked findings

1. **P1 — Must-fix: omitted evidence still passes citation validation.**  
   [analyst/prompt.py:109](/home/dev/.t3/worktrees/gemini-4-braincells/t3-d6675739-d37a5daea6e4e1c3/analyst/prompt.py:109) drops evidence without communicating the displayed IDs to [analyst/guard.py:19](/home/dev/.t3/worktrees/gemini-4-braincells/t3-d6675739-d37a5daea6e4e1c3/analyst/guard.py:19). Both analysis paths still validate against **all** context evidence.  
   **Reproduction:** after budget truncation hid IDs `1` and `2`, a fake draft citing them retained both citations, kept `llm_assessment="coordinated"`, and received no adjustments. Thus unseen IDs can satisfy the two-citation requirement.  
   **Fix:** return the displayed-ID set with the prompt and enforce against it. For tool-enabled investigation, additionally allow evidence actually returned through tools.

2. **P2 — Must-fix: media can crowd out all behavioural evidence and organic guards.**  
   [analyst/prompt.py:107](/home/dev/.t3/worktrees/gemini-4-braincells/t3-d6675739-d37a5daea6e4e1c3/analyst/prompt.py:107) consumes the budget in database order; [analyst/store.py:38](/home/dev/.t3/worktrees/gemini-4-braincells/t3-d6675739-d37a5daea6e4e1c3/analyst/store.py:38) orders by `kind, id`, putting media before signals.  
   **Reproduction:** sufficiently many long media rows displayed 15 media items but **zero signal items**, including no AGAINST evidence. The header’s aggregate scores do not replace those explanations or citable counter-evidence. The default four-media limit is per processing run, not a lifetime evidence-row cap.  
   **Fix:** reserve space for detector signals and organic guards first, then distribute the remainder across media and sources.

3. **P2 — Nice-to-have: unexpected programming errors become ordinary media failures.**  
   [media/nemotron.py:359](/home/dev/.t3/worktrees/gemini-4-braincells/t3-d6675739-d37a5daea6e4e1c3/media/nemotron.py:359) now catches SDK-call `TypeError`/`AttributeError` and wraps them in `NemotronError`. [media/worker.py:277](/home/dev/.t3/worktrees/gemini-4-braincells/t3-d6675739-d37a5daea6e4e1c3/media/worker.py:277) consequently treats them as recoverable per-image failures rather than surfacing the programming-error traceback.  
   **Verified:** ordinary programming errors get one attempt, not retries; `KeyboardInterrupt` propagates normally.  
   **Fix:** log every caught exception, but re-raise unexpected non-OpenAI exceptions unchanged; restrict retry classification to expected API failures.

4. **P3 — Nice-to-have: the per-item slice can cut structured evidence mid-string.**  
   [analyst/prompt.py:108](/home/dev/.t3/worktrees/gemini-4-braincells/t3-d6675739-d37a5daea6e4e1c3/analyst/prompt.py:108) slices **after** JSON serialization. Escaping can expand otherwise bounded fields.  
   **Reproduction:** a synthetic quote/backslash-heavy media item rendered to 4,890 characters and was cut to 4,000, leaving unterminated JSON and dropping trailing fields/provenance. **Its leading evidence ID remained intact**—I did not find a numeric-ID truncation ambiguity.  
   **Fix:** reduce field budgets until the complete serialized record fits, rather than slicing the serialized line.

### Other requested checks

- **Model guard:** both supplied real IDs pass; text-only Super, Nano VL and unrelated VL IDs fail. It checks family tokens, **not specifically version 3.5**; a synthetic `nemotron-2-super-vl` also passes. Use explicit normalized aliases if exact-version attestation is required.
- **OCR injection:** OCR is JSON-quoted and the system instruction explicitly treats image text as untrusted. No deterministic role-boundary escape found. Semantic prompt-injection remains a residual risk to explanations/tool choices; no live adversarial Gemini evaluation was performed.
- **Deployment check:** Python fallback and jq paths pass, including quiet/no-media cases and unavailable media responses. Media warnings do not fail deployment. The script does not enable `errexit`, and Trackdown’s grep uses a here-string, avoiding curl/grep SIGPIPE interactions. Advisory sampling can nevertheless add up to **120 seconds** under slow responses.
- **Logging:** new attempt records contain metadata, not credentials, OCR, image payloads or exception bodies. No new direct secret leak found; existing worker logging still prints exception messages.

"""Checks applied to every model draft before it is stored.

The detector decides; the model explains (PLAN section 5 proposal, implemented here):
`Verdict.status` is always the detector's status. The model's own call goes to `llm_assessment`,
with `agrees_with_detector` and `disagreement_reason`, so a disagreement is visible and counted
instead of overriding the detector. Each change guard makes is recorded in `Verdict.adjustments`.
"""

from analyst.context import ClusterContext
from analyst.verdict import Verdict, VerdictDraft

MIN_CITATIONS = 2


def enforce(draft: VerdictDraft, ctx: ClusterContext, *, model: str) -> Verdict:
    notes: list[str] = []
    assessment = draft.status

    known = ctx.evidence_ids
    unique = {c.evidence_id: c for c in reversed(draft.evidence)}  # first "why" wins
    cited = [unique[i] for i in dict.fromkeys(c.evidence_id for c in draft.evidence) if i in known]
    dropped = sorted({c.evidence_id for c in draft.evidence} - known)
    if dropped:
        notes.append(f"Dropped citations to unknown evidence ids {dropped}.")

    reason = draft.disagreement_reason.strip()
    if assessment != "insufficient" and len(cited) < MIN_CITATIONS:
        notes.append(
            f"Fewer than {MIN_CITATIONS} valid citations; the model's assessment "
            f"'{assessment}' was downgraded to 'insufficient'."
        )
        assessment = "insufficient"
        reason = reason or f"Fewer than {MIN_CITATIONS} valid citations."

    agrees = assessment == ctx.status
    if agrees:
        reason = ""
    elif not reason:
        reason = "The model gave no reason."
        notes.append("The model disagreed with the detector without giving a reason.")

    confidence = min(max(draft.confidence, 0.0), 1.0)
    if confidence != draft.confidence:
        notes.append("Confidence clamped to [0, 1].")

    if assessment == "coordinated" and not draft.counter_evidence:
        notes.append("The model offered no counter-evidence.")

    return Verdict(
        status=ctx.status,
        confidence=confidence,
        summary=draft.summary,
        evidence=cited,
        counter_evidence=draft.counter_evidence,
        would_change_verdict=draft.would_change_verdict,
        disagreement_reason=reason,
        model=model,
        detector_status=ctx.status,
        adjustments=notes,
        cluster_updated_at=ctx.updated_at,

"""One verdict for one cluster: prompt -> model draft -> guard.

`analyze` is the single-shot path (pre-gathered context only). `investigate` lets Gemini call
tools first (analyst/agent.py); evidence the tools store joins the cluster context before guard,
so the verdict may cite it and nothing else.
"""

from dataclasses import asdict, replace

from analyst.agent import GeminiAgent
from analyst.context import ClusterContext
from analyst.gemini import VerdictModel
from analyst.guard import enforce, no_evidence_verdict
from analyst.prompt import SYSTEM, build_prompt
from analyst.tools import ToolBox
from analyst.verdict import Verdict


def analyze(ctx: ClusterContext, model: VerdictModel) -> Verdict:
    if not ctx.evidence:
        return no_evidence_verdict(ctx)
    draft = model.draft(SYSTEM, build_prompt(ctx))
    return enforce(draft, ctx, model=model.name)


def investigate(ctx: ClusterContext, agent: GeminiAgent, tools: ToolBox) -> Verdict:
    if not ctx.evidence:
        return no_evidence_verdict(ctx)
    result = agent.run(SYSTEM, build_prompt(ctx), tools)
    full = replace(ctx, evidence=[*ctx.evidence, *tools.new_evidence.values()])
    verdict = enforce(result.draft, full, model=agent.name)
    return verdict.model_copy(
        update={
            "tool_calls": [asdict(r) for r in tools.records],
            "model_calls": [asdict(c) for c in result.model_calls],
            "cost_usd": result.cost_usd,
        }
    )

I'm planning a `fit_evidence` function in prompt.py that returns a copy of the cluster context with the evidence trimmed to fit the budget. Signals come first, then sources, then media, and each line gets its fields shrunk before rendering rather than cut after serialization. `build_prompt` would call the selection itself and add an omitted-items note when anything gets dropped.

| 8 | **Partially fixed** | Entry-point gates work, including zero-budget requests, but do not bound in-flight calls, retries, or all subsequent calls. Nested executor shutdown still waits. [service.py:310](/srv/junction-espoo/gemini-4-braincells.worktrees/dev-lookup/lookup/service.py:310), [service.py:939](/srv/junction-espoo/gemini-4-braincells.worktrees/dev-lookup/lookup/service.py:939) |

[Caddyfile:7](/srv/junction-espoo/gemini-4-braincells.worktrees/dev-lookup/deploy/Caddyfile:7), [lookup.py:84](/srv/junction-espoo/gemini-4-braincells.worktrees/dev-lookup/api/routes/lookup.py:84) |
| 10 | **Fixed** | Escaped underscores are normalized before avatar/handle parsing. [xpage.py:205](/srv/junction-espoo/gemini-4-braincells.worktrees/dev-lookup/lookup/xpage.py:205) |

## Ranked issues

### 1. P1 — NEW: completed results remain mutable — must-fix
[service.py:351](/srv/junction-espoo/gemini-4-braincells.worktrees/dev-lookup/lookup/service.py:351)

`shutdown(wait=False, cancel_futures=True)` does not stop running tasks. After a phase timeout, `_finish_graph`, assessment, and terminal-state publication can happen before those tasks update the result.

**Reproduced offline:** the lookup returned `done` with zero posts; releasing the blocked scrape subsequently added two posts while `origin_id` and `spread` remained null. Clients stop polling at `done`, and outstanding work no longer counts toward the running-job limit.

**Fix:** enforce deadline-aware I/O and cancellation, and prevent unfinished workers from publishing after finalization. Final graph/assessment must use a stable snapshot.

### 2. P1 — Residual #2: unread web snippets become origins — must-fix
[service.py:863](/srv/junction-espoo/gemini-4-braincells.worktrees/dev-lookup/lookup/service.py:863), [service.py:1315](/srv/junction-espoo/gemini-4-braincells.worktrees/dev-lookup/lookup/service.py:1315)

Web hits become `reference` pages from snippet similarity alone. An older date hint then qualifies that page as the origin without fetching it.

**Reproduced offline:** a November 1 snippet displaced a verified November 13 submitted post as `origin_id="page:1"`, with **zero page scrapes**.

**Fix:** retain these as candidate sources until their content and publication evidence are verified; an uncertainty interval does not verify the underlying snippet.

### 3. P1 — Residual #8: budget does not bound work/spending — must-fix
[service.py:708](/srv/junction-espoo/gemini-4-braincells.worktrees/dev-lookup/lookup/service.py:708), [service.py:939](/srv/junction-espoo/gemini-4-braincells.worktrees/dev-lookup/lookup/service.py:939), [oxylabs.py:190](/srv/junction-espoo/gemini-4-braincells.worktrees/dev-lookup/sources/oxylabs.py:190)

`author_feed` has no intervening gate, Oxylabs retries lack deadline checks, and provider timeouts are not clamped to remaining time. The verification pools’ context managers wait for running workers even after `map` times out.

**Reproduced offline:** `author_feed` started after expiry; verification remained blocked beyond its timeout until the mocked worker was released.

**Fix:** propagate an absolute deadline through each HTTP call/retry, gate every subsequent call, and remove blocking executor teardown from timeout paths.

### 4. P2 — NEW integration gap: Gemini loses match provenance — must-fix
[assess.py:83](/srv/junction-espoo/gemini-4-braincells.worktrees/dev-lookup/lookup/assess.py:83)

The assessment brief discards `match` and `verdict_applies`, sending only cluster ID, detector status, and score. With mixed applicable/account-only matches, the model cannot identify which cluster verdict applies. The account-only explanatory note is also omitted when any applicable cluster exists.

**Fix:** preserve per-cluster provenance in the brief and explicitly distinguish account context from applicable verdicts.

### 5. P2 — NEW integration gap: uncertain times display as exact — must-fix
[lookup.ts:216](/srv/junction-espoo/gemini-4-braincells.worktrees/dev-lookup/web/trackdown/src/data/lookup.ts:216)

The frontend ignores `time_uncertainty_s`, marks a date-only page’s midnight timestamp as known, and displays no uncertainty flag.

**Reproduced:** a 24-hour search-hint interval rendered as **“13 Nov 2026 · 00:00”**, with `timeUnknown=false` and no flags.

**Fix:** carry precision into frontend types and render date-only/range labels rather than an exact clock time.

**Nice-to-have — direct deployment hardening:** [Caddyfile:7](/srv/junction-espoo/gemini-4-braincells.worktrees/dev-lookup/deploy/Caddyfile:7) trusts every private-range caller. In base-compose deployments, a directly connecting private-network client can supply its own XFF and bypass the per-client cap. Scope proxy trust to the actual ingress, preferably through the VPS-specific configuration.

**Fix:** retain these as candidate sources until their content and publication evidence are verified; an uncertainty interval does not verify the underlying snippet.

### 3. P1 — Residual #8: budget does not bound work/spending — must-fix
[service.py:708](/srv/junction-espoo/gemini-4-braincells.worktrees/dev-lookup/lookup/service.py:708), [service.py:939](/srv/junction-espoo/gemini-4-braincells.worktrees/dev-lookup/lookup/service.py:939), [oxylabs.py:190](/srv/junction-espoo/gemini-4-braincells.worktrees/dev-lookup/sources/oxylabs.py:190)

`author_feed` has no intervening gate, Oxylabs retries lack deadline checks, and provider timeouts are not clamped to remaining time. The verification pools’ context managers wait for running workers even after `map` times out.

**Reproduced offline:** `author_feed` started after expiry; verification remained blocked beyond its timeout until the mocked worker was released.

**Fix:** propagate an absolute deadline through each HTTP call/retry, gate every subsequent call, and remove blocking executor teardown from timeout paths.

### 4. P2 — NEW integration gap: Gemini loses match provenance — must-fix
[assess.py:83](/srv/junction-espoo/gemini-4-braincells.worktrees/dev-lookup/lookup/assess.py:83)

The assessment brief discards `match` and `verdict_applies`, sending only cluster ID, detector status, and score. With mixed applicable/account-only matches, the model cannot identify which cluster verdict applies. The account-only explanatory note is also omitted when any applicable cluster exists.

**Fix:** preserve per-cluster provenance in the brief and explicitly distinguish account context from applicable verdicts.

### 5. P2 — NEW integration gap: uncertain times display as exact — must-fix
[lookup.ts:216](/srv/junction-espoo/gemini-4-braincells.worktrees/dev-lookup/web/trackdown/src/data/lookup.ts:216)

The frontend ignores `time_uncertainty_s`, marks a date-only page’s midnight timestamp as known, and displays no uncertainty flag.

**Reproduced:** a 24-hour search-hint interval rendered as **“13 Nov 2026 · 00:00”**, with `timeUnknown=false` and no flags.

**Fix:** carry precision into frontend types and render date-only/range labels rather than an exact clock time.

**Nice-to-have — direct deployment hardening:** [Caddyfile:7](/srv/junction-espoo/gemini-4-braincells.worktrees/dev-lookup/deploy/Caddyfile:7) trusts every private-range caller. In base-compose deployments, a directly connecting private-network client can supply its own XFF and bypass the per-client cap. Scope proxy trust to the actual ingress, preferably through the VPS-specific configuration.

For valid stored evidence, fitting cannot remove **all** items: each rendered line is capped at 4,000 characters, below the initial evidence budget. **Verdict: not approved yet.** Reviewed `65a9080`; the successful-path fixes work, but citation registration still has an error-path loophole.

**Previous Findings**
- **R2 #1 — partially fixed.** Verified with the real `ToolBox`: an omitted, stored source returned by a cached `scrape_url` becomes citable despite being absent from `new_evidence`. Both service and comparison merge returned evidence. The failure-path issue below remains; comparison also loses the full-context URL allowlist.
- **R2 #2 — fixed.** Refitting preserves `evidence_omitted`, including repeated fits.
- **R1 items — remain fixed:** prompt/guard fitting on successful paths, signal/organic-guard priority, bounded valid media JSON, programming-error re-raising versus API retry/wrapping, and the Nemotron **3.5** Super VL requirement.

**Newly Identified Issues**
1. **P2 — must-fix: evidence becomes citable before the tool successfully returns it.**  
   At [analyst/tools.py:402](/home/dev/.t3/worktrees/gemini-4-braincells/t3-d6675739-d37a5daea6e4e1c3/analyst/tools.py:402), `_remember()` runs before result processing. Reproduced using malformed stored search detail (`hits: [None]`): processing throws, `call()` returns only an error and records `ok=False`, yet the evidence remains in `returned` and the guard accepts a citation to it. This ordering predates the latest commit; the expanded whitelist inherits the problem.  
   **Fix:** register citable evidence only after constructing a successful response. Build the guard whitelist from successfully returned items—not all `new_evidence`, which can also retain failed attempts. Add an exception-after-fetch regression test.

2. **P3 — nice-to-have: comparison builds its URL allowlist from fitted evidence.**  
   At [analyst/compare.py:79](/home/dev/.t3/worktrees/gemini-4-braincells/t3-d6675739-d37a5daea6e4e1c3/analyst/compare.py:79), fitting happens before `ToolBox` construction. Reproduced a scrape of a URL present only in omitted stored evidence: comparison rejects it as “URL not allowed,” while production correctly permits it.  
   **Fix:** retain the full context for toolbox construction; use the fitted copy for the prompt and initial citation whitelist.

**Ownership And Validation**
- No cross-cluster evidence leak found in production paths: `DbSink` scopes reads/writes by cluster; shared `WebCache` stores content that is saved under the receiving cluster.
- Normal fetch failures, budget refusals, and blocked URLs leave `returned` empty. The first finding concerns exceptions **after** registration.
- Full suite, with pytest’s cache provider disabled: **303 passed, 8 skipped** in 22.43s. Additional in-memory reproductions passed. Working tree remains clean; no edits or remote actions.

    def call(self, name: str, args: dict) -> dict:
        """Run one tool call and return the function response for the model."""
        args = dict(args or {})
        started = time.monotonic()
        rec = ToolCallRecord(name=name, args=args, latency_ms=0, ok=False, why=args.get("why"))
        try:
            refusal = self.budget.refusal()
            if refusal:
                rec.error = refusal
                return {"error": refusal + "; write your verdict with what you have"}
            handler: Callable[[dict, ToolCallRecord], dict] | None = {

                "scrape_url": self._scrape_url,
                "get_cluster_posts": self._get_cluster_posts,
                "get_account": self._get_account,
            }.get(name)
            if handler is None or name not in {d["name"] for d in self.declarations()}:
                rec.error = f"unknown tool {name}"  # not counted against the budget
                return {"error": rec.error}
            self.budget.tool_calls += 1
            try:
                out = handler(args, rec)
            except BudgetRefused as exc:
                rec.error = str(exc)
                return {"error": f"{exc}; write your verdict with what you have"}
            except Exception as exc:  # a broken tool must not cost the cluster its verdict

content.thinking:
I'm going to drop the change to `_remember` that writes into `returned` and stop it from adding anything there. Instead, once a call succeeds and its output includes an evidence_id that was remembered earlier, I'll store the item under that id in `returned`. The item has to come from somewhere, and `ToolCallRecord` is a dataclass that `asdict` relies on, so I won't add a field to it. I'll keep the item in a local dict instead.

I'm settling on the fix for `returned`: in `call()`, I'll reset a `_last_item` marker before each handler and, on success, store the item under its id. In service and compare, `returned` will hold only what was actually returned, kept separate from `new_evidence`, and compare will keep the full context separate from the fitted one.

The fix makes an item citable only after its tool call succeeds, so the guard's whitelist comes solely from successful returns. I'm now building the toolbox from the full context in the compare script.

def test_evidence_is_citable_only_after_the_tool_call_succeeded():
    from analyst.context import EvidenceItem
    from analyst.tools import Budget, ToolBox

    class Sink:
        pass

    box = ToolBox(ctx(), web=None, sink=Sink(), cache=None,
                  budget=Budget(max_tool_calls=5, max_web_calls=5, max_seconds=60))
    item = EvidenceItem(id=777, kind="source", summary="s", detail={}, source_url=None,
                        model="oxylabs")

    def broken(args, rec):
        box._remember(item, rec)
        raise ValueError("processing failed after the fetch")

    def fine(args, rec):
        box._remember(item, rec)
        return {"evidence_id": item.id}

    box._search_web = broken
    box.call("search_web", {"query": "q"})
    assert 777 not in box.returned
    box._search_web = fine
    box.call("search_web", {"query": "q"})
